cases.title: SIM Cards Not Connecting — Matcha Electric (USC DS3 Circuit Issue)
cases.findings: USC DS3 circuit drops causing Delete Session Requests on Plantsville, CT SIMs. Disconnection rate 92%+ on worst SIM. Brooklyn SIM shows normal ~5.37% SGSN timeout behavior (different failure mode). USC escalation CW-3824 — rep Dylan Dreiling noted they can't get responses from their own roaming support. JIRA escalated.
cases.notes: Sensei-assisted analysis. Investigated Brooklyn ICCID ...1410 — confirmed different failure pattern than Plantsville. Brooklyn = normal SGSN timeouts; Plantsville = roaming partner core transport failures. Same carrier (MCC 310/MNC 410), same IMSI5 profile, but fundamentally different root causes.
cases.response: Awaiting USC repair on DS3 circuit. JIRA CW-3824.

cases.title: Outbound Busy Signal Investigation — Ringba
cases.findings: Outbound calls getting busy signal; client's call center says calls never reached them. SIP analysis of 5 call legs shows: initial carrier gateway 503 errors, then 603 Decline from far end, then eventual success on final attempt. The 'busy' = destination actively declining (603 Decline). Carrier gateways returning 503 on initial attempts also concerning. Client uses sequential dialing (tries multiple targets).
cases.notes: Sensei-assisted SIP analysis. 5 UUIDs analyzed. Key finding: 603 Decline from far end = destination rejecting, not network issue. 503 from carrier gateways on initial attempts = pre-routing rejection. Call center may have PBX auto-reject or queue capacity limits.
cases.response: SIP analysis shared — recommend client check PBX/ACD auto-reject rules and queue capacity.
